Getting started with bwTools

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Overview

bwTools uses one stable data flow for BigWig, WIG, and bedGraph signal tracks:

file -> read_bwg() -> BwgTrack -> analysis -> write_bwg()

Public coordinates are always 1-based closed.

Load the bundled example 

library(bwTools)

bw_file <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "bwtools_example.bigwig",
  package = "bwTools",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

bw <- read_bwg(bw_file, sample_ids = "example")

A BigWig-only input uses lazy indexed access by default. Inspect the track with summary_bwg(), samples_bwg(), seqinfo_bwg(), metadata_bwg(), and zoominfo_bwg():

summary_bwg(bw)
samples_bwg(bw)
seqinfo_bwg(bw)
metadata_bwg(bw)
zoominfo_bwg(bw)

Use is_bwg_track() for a logical contract check and validate_bwg() when an invalid object should raise an error:

is_bwg_track(bw)
validate_bwg(bw)

Retrieve a region 

region <- retrieve_bwg(
  bw,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 500L,
  end = 1600L
)

Request result = "track" when the result will be passed to another bwTools operation:

region_track <- retrieve_bwg(
  bw,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 500L,
  end = 1600L,
  result = "track"
)

Calculate statistics 

stats_bwg(
  bw,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 1L,
  end = 10000L,
  n_bins = 20L,
  stat = "mean",
  use_zoom = FALSE
)

Use use_zoom = TRUE for fast large-region summaries when approximate boundary handling from stored BigWig zoom windows is acceptable.

Merge tracks

merge_bwg() conservatively preserves sample identity with method = "auto":

a <- retrieve_bwg(bw, "chr1", 500L, 900L, result = "track")
b <- retrieve_bwg(bw, "chr1", 1200L, 1600L, result = "track")
merged <- merge_bwg(a, b)

Use method = "mean" or method = "sum" only when arithmetic aggregation is intended.

Write a result 

manifest <- write_bwg(
  region_track,
  outdir = "bwtools-output",
  format = "bigwig",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

write_bwg() is the only normal signal-file persistence function. The returned manifest has one row per selected written sample.

Constructing a BwgTrack directly

Use bwg_track() when signal data already exist in R:

x <- bwg_track(
  samples = data.frame(sample_id = "sampleA"),
  data = data.frame(
    sample_id = "sampleA",
    chrom = "chr1",
    start = 1L,
    end = 10L,
    value = 2,
    strand = "+"
  ),
  seqinfo = data.frame(chrom = "chr1", length = 1000L)
)

The in-memory signal schema is sample_id, chrom, start, end, value, and strand.
